data.description:
Board request, verbatim (DM msg 367, 2026-09-01): 'urls in chat messages should resolve to links, like http://127.0.0.1:8348/ should be clickable'. Today only markdown-style links work — bare URLs render as literal text.

RENDER PATH (the real one, read before planning): message bodies are rendered client-side in apps/chat/public/app.js bodyNode() as a structure-first pipeline (AS-26 §6): tokenizeInline (apps/chat/public/markdown.js) over the whole body, then appendRefLeaf() runs three pure ref passes over every plain-text leaf in fixed order — AS-refs, msg-refs (tokenizeMsgRefs), file-refs (tokenizeFileRefs, both in apps/chat/public/msg-refs.js). Zero innerHTML anywhere; tokenizers emit text and structure, NEVER markup; DOM assembly is el()/createTextNode only. Markdown links [label](https://…) already work via the 'link' pattern in markdown.js with an http/https-only scheme allowlist.

THE WORK: a new pure tokenizer pass (tokenizeUrls or similar — pure module, no DOM/fetch/globals, importable from node:test, same pattern as msg-refs.js) that finds BARE absolute URLs in plain-text leaves and emits url tokens; app.js renders them as anchors with target=_blank rel=noopener, href set only from the matched slice.

SCOPE BOUNDARY (CTO calls, bake into the plan):
- http:// and https:// ONLY — same allowlist as markdown.js links. No scheme-less www. guessing, no mailto, and javascript:/data: etc. must be structurally impossible (fail the match, stay literal).
- Trailing-punctuation trim: sentence punctuation (. , ; : ! ?) at the URL end stays literal text; a trailing ')' is part of the URL only if a matching '(' occurs inside it (the '(see http://x/)' idiom).
- Round-trip invariant holds: concatenating token texts reproduces the input exactly.
- Runs on code-span inners too — consistent with the deliberate file-ref precedent (a backticked URL is a common idiom here).
- Ordering vs existing passes: verify no partial-capture interaction with FILE_RE (its lookbehind should already reject path segments inside URLs — prove it in tests, e.g. https://github.com/x/blob/main/README.md must yield ONE url token, no fileref) and with msg-ref continuation lists.
- Nested-anchor hazard: appendRefLeaf also runs on md-link inners (app.js line ~223). The URL pass must not build an <a> inside an existing <a> — decide the mechanism in the plan (skip the pass for link inners, or render as plain text there).

Tests in apps/chat/test following the existing node:test tokenizer-test pattern. Server, store, exports, and CLI output are untouched — this is a client render-path change only.
data.title: Chat: autolink bare http/https URLs in message bodies

data.body: Implementer note — the one thing not to get wrong: this surface renders text authored by both agents and the human, and the app's entire XSS posture is structural (no innerHTML, no sanitizer — safety comes from tokenizers that never emit markup and DOM built with el()/textContent). Keep it that way: the new pass emits {type:'url', text, href} tokens where href is byte-identical to the matched source slice, and the scheme allowlist lives in the REGEX (like markdown.js PATTERNS), not in a post-hoc check. Do not introduce innerHTML, do not 'normalize' or decode the href, and do not add a sanitizer library — any of those is plan-level rework on sight. Pull-order note: board-requested internal tool; slots into the internal line after AS-34 and AS-27, ahead of cosmetics (AS-32/28/33). Does not preempt the D1 build line.
Board directive (DM msg 394): all chat issues ship. Cluster order 3/6 — board-requested (msg 367); ordering per my msg 373 commitment: after AS-34/AS-27, ahead of cosmetics.

Pulled while AS-45 waits on the board. Cluster item 2/6 in the order recorded on AS-34, and a board request in the board member's own words (DM msg 367).

WHY THIS RATHER THAN A UI TASK, and it is a finding worth recording rather than a scheduling note. On the graph, AS-46, AS-47 and AS-48 are all unblocked — their depends_on edges point at AS-42, AS-43, AS-44, AS-30 and AS-65, every one of them done. In practice all three are blocked on AS-45, and the graph does not say so. They inherit its view layer: the four lexical guards, the token check, the render conventions, and the README section three planners were repeatedly told to read first. Starting one now would mean branching either from master, where none of that exists and it would be duplicated, or from an unmerged branch sitting under a fired safety valve. Neither is a real option.

So the D1 UI tier is blocked on a decision, not on work, and that changes the cost of one of the courses put to the board: merging AS-45 now and filing its findings unblocks three tasks, while a fourth review cycle keeps three tasks waiting on a two-character fix. That was not visible when the courses were written and the board should have it.

The dependency edges should probably say this. I am not adding them unilaterally — a depends_on edge from three tasks to AS-45 changes the graph the ready-queue is computed from, and the milestone plan's section 8 built that graph deliberately. Recorded for the CTO.

CHAT IS THE RIGHT SURFACE MEANWHILE: apps/chat shares no file with the unmerged invoicing branch, so nothing started here can collide with it, and the internal-tools kickoff is implicit per CLAUDE.md.

Marcus keeps it — he is already the assignee, he wrote the render path this touches, and rotating an assignee mid-queue for its own sake costs context for nothing.

Plan written (~5k words; small task, short plan). Design spiked before writing: the 13 real URL occurrences in chat history drive the boundary rules, and the three cross-pass collisions are MEASURED, not assumed — FILE_RE fires on query-position .md (https://example.com/?f=README.md yields a fileref today), HEAD_RE fires on http://host/msg156, and \bAS-26\b fires inside a URL path. That makes URL-first mandatory, not tidy: the URL pass runs first and its tokens are terminal, so no other pass can ever observe text inside a URL's slice. Scheme allowlist is http/https lowercase only, in the regex, byte-parity with markdown.js, enforced by a parity test. Double-linking is impossible by two structural facts: a md-link's href is never a leaf, and appendRefLeaf gains {autolink:false} at the md-link call site so the pass is not called there at all. tokenizeUrls lives in markdown.js (not a new module, not msg-refs.js) — no STATIC_FILES entry, and the two scheme allowlists sit on one screen. Fuzz: 200k inputs, 81,213 url tokens, 0 violations of round-trip/slice-identity/href-identity/scheme/charset. §6 predicted failing sets were VERIFIED against mutated spikes and I corrected myself twice — the fuzz test does not fail under the pass-order mutation, and the escaped-literal baselines were wrong when run through eval. Honest limit recorded in §8 Q6: no jsdom, so the DOM assembly is a lexical guard on the served app.js plus inspection, and the plan says what that does and does not establish. 12 ACs, 9 new tests, ~55 lines of production code.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-54 on feat/AS-54-autolink, per the plan: tokenizeUrls in markdown.js with the scheme allowlist at byte parity, the fixed-point trailing trim, URL-pass-first with terminal tokens so no ref pass can observe text inside a URL, and the autolink flag that makes an anchor inside a markdown-link label unreachable rather than unlikely.

Implementation complete — AS-54, branch feat/AS-54-autolink, commits 045cabf (code+tests) and 374fbc9 (README). Both independently green; worktree clean. FILES TOUCHED (exactly the five in plan §2; nothing else in the repo changed) apps/chat/public/markdown.js +66/-1 URL_RE, SENTENCE_TAIL, BRACKETS, count(), trimUrlTail(), tokenizeUrls(); header comment apps/chat/public/app.js +50/-16 urlLink(); appendRefLeaf gains { autolink = true } = {}; import; two comment updates; one call-site change apps/chat/test/markdown.test.js +207/-2 8 new tests (AC-1..AC-8), imports apps/chat/test/api.test.js +32/-0 1 new test (AC-9) apps/chat/README.md +15/-0 one paragraph in the inline-markdown section TOTAL 366 insertions, 22 deletions across 5 files. app.js is bigger than the plan's "+14, ~4 modified" estimate purely because wrapping the existing body in the URL loop re-indents it one level; the behavioural diff is byte-for-byte the plan's §3.8 snippet. Not a design deviation, just estimate-vs-measured. SUITE Before (at 220ac8b, in the worktree): tests 194, pass 194, fail 0. After (at 374fbc9): tests 203, pass 203, fail 0. = AC-10 exactly (194 + 8 + 1). No pre-existing test changed state. AC-12: apps/chat/package.json unchanged — zero dependencies added. Confirmed UNCHANGED alongside msg-refs.js, style.css, server.js, compose.yaml, Dockerfile (the plan's not-moving set, below). LITERALS THAT MOVED — every row of plan §4, measured with `grep -oF … | wc -l` (never grep -c) markdown.js https?:\/\/ 1 -> 2 (link pattern + URL_RE) markdown.js tokenizeUrls 0 -> exported (1 `export function`) app.js appendRefLeaf( 4 -> 4 (1 definition + 3 calls; no new call sites) app.js { autolink: false } 0 -> 1 app.js urlLink 0 -> 2 (definition + one call) markdown.test.js ^test( 10 -> 18 api.test.js ^test( 25 -> 26 app.js .innerHTML 0 -> 0 | bare innerHTML 2 -> 2 (both comments — the plan's grep trap; I grepped `.innerHTML`) NOT-MOVING SET, confirmed by per-file `git diff --quiet`: msg-refs.js UNCHANGED (HEAD_RE/CONT_RE/FILE_RE untouched — the query-position FILE_RE collision is neutralised by pass order, not by widening a lookbehind), style.css UNCHANGED, server.js UNCHANGED, package.json UNCHANGED, compose.yaml UNCHANGED, Dockerfile UNCHANGED. markdown.js PATTERNS still 5 entries. app.js appendInlineToken untouched (2 occurrences, not in the diff). `git diff --stat master...HEAD` lists five files and no others. MUTATION TESTING — one indivisible step per recipe, run against a `git archive HEAD` extract at $SCRATCH/mut (494 files, verified green at 203 before any mutation), backups/manifests outside the extract. The task worktree was never mutated. The harness asserts the mutation applied on disk and aborts before running node --test on any count mismatch. F1 — scheme allowlist is load-bearing. URL_RE `https?:\/\/` -> `[a-z]+:\/\/`. assert-applied: markdown.js `[a-z]+:\/\/` 0 -> 1 ; `https?:\/\/` 2 -> 1 (the link pattern's copy survives). Both matched. predicted 3, observed 3, IDENTICAL SET: urls: scheme allowlist — non-http(s) schemes never produce a url token urls: scheme parity — bare URLs and markdown links accept the same schemes urls: href is a verbatim source slice; round-trip holds over a fuzz corpus totals 203/200 pass/3 fail. Corpus, punctuation, bracket and pass-order tests PASSED under F1, exactly as the plan says they should — they never look at the scheme. The fuzz test DID fail, which is the non-http salt in the generator doing its job. Classification: CONFIRMED — the allowlist is guarded, not decorative. F3a — the autolink:false guard is not vacuous. Deleted `, { autolink: false }` at app.js:249. assert-applied: `{ autolink: false }` 1 -> 0 ; `appendRefLeaf(` still 4. Both matched. predicted 1, observed 1, IDENTICAL: api: AS-54 — served app.js autolinks through markdown.js and never inside a markdown link. totals 203/202/1. Classification: CONFIRMED. F3b — pass order inside appendRefLeaf is not vacuous. Inverted the nesting so tokenizeAsRefs is the outer loop and tokenizeUrls the inner one. (The plan says "swap the two lines"; in the real code they are not sibling lines but nested loops, so the smallest true order-inversion is the nesting swap. Recorded as deviation 3.) assert-applied, SCOPED to the appendRefLeaf body: tokenizeAsRefs@93 now precedes tokenizeUrls@195. predicted 1, observed 1, IDENTICAL: the same api test. totals 203/202/1. Classification: CONFIRMED. F4 — full-URL matching / pass order is load-bearing. URL_RE excluded set `\\]*` -> `\\\/]*` (match stops at the first `/` after the host). assert-applied: markdown.js `\/]*` 0 -> 1 (matched, this is the plan's primary assert). predicted 4, observed 4, IDENTICAL SET: urls: bare http/https autolink — the corpus cases from chat history urls: trailing sentence punctuation stays literal text urls: closing brackets belong to the URL only when balanced urls: pass order — refs inside a URL are never linkified; refs outside still are totals 203/199/4. The fuzz test did NOT fail — matching the CTO's warning and NOT my own prior expectation-free run; a shorter match preserves round-trip, slice identity, scheme and charset. Classification: CONFIRMED, prediction exact including the negative one. RESTORATION PROOF: fresh extract re-taken after every recipe and diffed against the pristine content-hash manifest — identical, 494 files. Worktree apps/chat content-hash manifest identical before/after (78 files). `git -C .worktrees/AS-54 status --porcelain` = 0 lines. F2 — ADVERSARIAL: attempting to get markup or a live handler out of a message body. No mutation; the plan's 16 payloads through the real tokenizer. 16 payloads examined, 0 violations. Emitted href bytes (this is the ONLY string that ever reaches an attribute; everything else goes through createTextNode/textContent): 1 javascript:alert(1) -> 0 url tokens, no anchor constructed 2 JaVaScRiPt:alert(1) -> 0 3 javascript:alert(1) -> 0 4 data:text/html, -> 0 5 vbscript:msgbox(1) -> 0 6 http://x/" onmouseover="alert(1) -> 1, href "http://x/" (9 B, 687474703a2f2f782f) 7 http://x/'> -> 1, href "http://x/" (9 B) 8 http://x/ -> 1, href "http://x/" (9 B) 10 http://x/#

Orchestrator verification and review assignment.

VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY: exactly the five files plan section 2 declares, nothing else in the branch diff. msg-refs.js, style.css and server.js are untouched, which matters because the query-position collision is neutralised by pass order rather than by widening a lookbehind that would change file-ref behaviour outside URLs too. The parked AS-45 worktree is undisturbed at f24a3bb, and both long-running containers are up and healthy.

THE IMPLEMENTER FOUND A DEFECT IN THE PLAN'S OWN FALSIFICATION SECTION, and it is the kind that would have produced a false green. F3's second-half assert-applied one-liner compares two whole-file indices; run against the UNMUTATED file it prints an ordering that satisfies the assertion and exits 0. It reports "the swap took" with nothing mutated. He replaced it with a scoped assert inside the function body and said so rather than running the recipe as written and reporting a pass.

That is the same shape as the trap the plan itself warned about one paragraph earlier — the bare-word grep that reads a clean file as a violation — arriving from the opposite direction. A whole-file index comparison is vacuous for the same reason a whole-file token count is: the subject of the assertion is not the thing the mutation changes. Worth generalising: an assert-applied step must be scoped to the region the mutation edits, not to the file that contains it.

He also corrected the plan's stated direction on one baseline (measured the reverse of what section 6 claims) and applied the same scoping fix to an acceptance criterion whose comparison was vacuous for the identical reason — one function is defined above the other, so a whole-file comparison passes regardless.

THE CTO'S NEGATIVE PREDICTION HELD. He predicted, after running it, that the pass-order mutation would NOT redden the fuzz case because a shorter match preserves every invariant, and warned the implementer not to predict it. Observed: the fuzz case passed under that mutation. A negative prediction confirmed is worth as much as a positive one and is rarer.

ADVERSARIAL RESULTS ARE CLEAN AND REPORTED AS BYTES rather than as a pass: the five script-scheme payloads produce zero url tokens, so no anchor is constructed at all rather than being constructed and then rejected; the host-confusion string yields the honest host; fullwidth scheme characters yield nothing. 50,000 fuzz inputs, 28,210 url tokens, zero violations against a floor of 10,000.

THE DOM LIMIT IS STATED IN THE PLAN'S OWN WORDS and not upgraded: the tokenizer is executed, DOM assembly is a lexical guard on the served file plus inspection, and he says explicitly that it does not prove the browser builds no nested anchor. He booted a server on an ephemeral port to read the served bytes rather than the source file, which is the right instrument for a claim about what the browser receives.

REVIEW: assigning agent:qa-priya. Marcus implemented, so implementer != reviewer holds. Priya over Ruben because Ruben has spent three cycles inside the invoicing view layer and this is a different app with a different safety property; a reader without that framing is more likely to probe the boundary rules as a person would type them rather than as a guard set. She also has not read this app's render path, which is the point.

QA review — AS-54, branch feat/AS-54-autolink at 374fbc9, reviewed cold in .worktrees/AS-54. VERDICT: implementation-level rework needed. AC verdict: 11 of 12 pass. AC-9 fails: one of its five clauses is a vacuous guard that passes against an implementation that does not do the thing the criterion names. The plan is sound and needs no change; the fix is confined to apps/chat/test/api.test.js. READ ORDER (disclosed): CLAUDE.md Review Gate + Review Rework Loop; PHILOSOPHY.md; my dossier; the plan in full (625 lines); the task description alone via `lattice show AS-54 --json` piped through node to print `description`. Then the diff cold, then the two test files as documents. Then I ran everything and wrote my verdicts and failing sets down. I read the seven-comment stream LAST, after all measurement was recorded; differences from it are at the end. WHAT I RAN, WITH CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION - Suite, 3 trees: master (194/194), 045cabf (203/203), 374fbc9 (203/203). Trees extracted with `git archive` into scratch; both commits independently green; baseline 194 confirmed, not taken on trust. 203 = 194 + 8 + 1. - 12 mutation recipes: the plan's 4 (F1, F3a, F3b, F4) re-derived independently with my own mutation shapes, plus 8 of my own (P1-P8). Every one against a fresh `git archive HEAD` extract outside the worktree; assert-applied scoped to the edited region (this task's own finding), harness aborts on an unapplied mutation rather than reporting. - 61 adversarial inputs through the real tokenizer (the plan's F2 16 + 45 of mine), 46 url tokens. - The real chat corpus: 502 messages, 9 containing a URL, 13 URL occurrences, driven through the FULL pipeline (tokenizeInline, then tokenizeUrls per plain leaf with md-link inners skipped). - Fuzz re-derivation from the committed generator: 50,000 inputs, 28,210 url tokens, 14,566 distinct hrefs, 38,240 non-http salt pieces across 26,346 inputs. - A future-pass probe: 4 inputs, 11 candidate matches lying inside URLs, 0 leaked. - 3 first-hand checks of plan §6 text against the real file. - Ports: every server I booted used port 0 (ephemeral). asc-chat-server-1 (8347) and asc-invoicing-web-1 (8348) were never touched. .worktrees/AS-45 left at f24a3bb, porcelain empty. PER-AC VERDICT AC-1 corpus cases PASS reddens under F4 and P5/P6 AC-2 trailing sentence punctuation PASS reddens under F4 and P5 AC-3 balanced brackets PASS reddens under F4 and P6 AC-4 scheme allowlist PASS reddens under F1 AC-5 scheme parity bare vs markdown PASS reddens under F1 AC-6 fuzz, verbatim slice, round-trip PASS 28,210 url tokens vs a 10,000 floor; reddens under F1 AC-7 pass order composition PASS reddens under F4 (limit noted below, accepted by plan) AC-8 junk tolerance PASS AC-9 served app.js lexical guard FAIL 4 of 5 clauses proven non-vacuous; 1 vacuous (D1) AC-10 suite 203/203, baseline 194 PASS measured on all three trees; no pre-existing test changed state AC-11 README paragraph PASS all five required statements present AC-12 no new dependency PASS package.json byte-identical; no lockfile, no node_modules RECIPES — PREDICTED vs OBSERVED (12; every assert-applied scoped to the edited region) F1 URL_RE https?:// -> [a-z]+:// assert-applied: within the `const URL_RE =` line only, `[a-z]+:\/\/` present, `https?:\/\/` gone. predicted 3 / observed 3, EXACT: scheme allowlist; scheme parity; fuzz. 200 pass / 3 fail. Classification: CONFIRMED. The allowlist is load-bearing, and the non-http salt in the fuzz generator is what makes the fuzz case see it. F3a delete `, { autolink: false }` at the md-link call site assert-applied: scoped to the `if (tok.type === 'link')` block. predicted 1 / observed 1, EXACT: the AS-54 api test. 202 pass / 1 fail. CONFIRMED. F3b invert the nesting so tokenizeAsRefs is the outer loop assert-applied: within the appendRefLeaf body only, tokenizeAsRefs now precedes tokenizeUrls. predicted 1 / observed 1, EXACT: the AS-54 api test. 202 pass / 1 fail. CONFIRMED. F4 URL_RE excluded set gains \/ (match stops at the first path slash) assert-applied: within the `const URL_RE =` line only, `\\\/]*` present, `\\]*` gone. predicted 4 / observed 4, EXACT: corpus; punctuation; brackets; pass order. 199 pass / 4 fail. THE NEGATIVE PREDICTION HOLDS, verified first-hand: the fuzz case did NOT redden. It is absent from the observed failing set of four. A shorter match preserves round-trip, slice identity, href identity, ^https?://[A-Za-z0-9] and the excluded charset — every invariant AC-6 asserts. The fuzz test is exactly as strong as claimed and no stronger, which is why AC-1/2/3 must exist beside it. CONFIRMED, including the negative half. P1 urlLink stops setting href at all (my recipe) assert-applied: within the urlLink body only, `a.href = tok.href;` gone, el() call intact. predicted 1 / observed 0. 203 pass / 0 fail. >>> VACUOUS GUARD. See D1. P2 urlLink transforms the href: a.href = decodeURIComponent(tok.href) (my recipe) assert-applied: within the urlLink body only, decodeURIComponent present. predicted 1 / observed 0. 203 pass / 0 fail. >>> Same vacuity, from the other direction: the plan's implementer note calls a decoded href plan-level rework on sight, and nothing catches it. P3 url tokens stop being terminal — delete the `continue` after appendChild(urlLink(u)) (my recipe) assert-applied: within the appendRefLeaf body only. predicted 0 (probe) / observed 0. 203 pass / 0 fail. See D2. P4 delete `URL_RE.lastIndex = last` (my recipe) — the line whose own comment says REQUIRED predicted unstated (measuring) / observed 0. 203 pass / 0 fail. See D3. P5 SENTENCE_TAIL '.,;:!?' -> '.,;:!' (my recipe) observed 2: corpus cases; trailing sentence punctuation. The trim set is guarded. P6 bracket balance `>` -> `>=` (my recipe) observed 2: corpus cases; closing brackets. The bracket rule is guarded. P7 reintroduce `.innerHTML` into app.js (my recipe) observed 2: the AS-54 api test AND the pre-existing AS-26 served-modules test. The house rule has defence in depth. Non-vacuous. P8 app.js stops importing tokenizeUrls from markdown.js and inlines a private stub (my recipe) observed 1, EXACT: the AS-54 api test. The one-allowlist-one-module clause is non-vacuous. RESTORATION, PROVEN: content-hash manifest over the worktree's 78 tracked apps/chat files, sha256 d46868832514df183c882491d5366a575b16b4646623dfb423a2f55557137686, identical before and after all 12 recipes; `git -C .worktrees/AS-54 status --porcelain` = 0 lines. Every mutation lived in a scratch extract that was deleted after each recipe. `grep -c` was not used anywhere in the harness; occurrence counts are `grep -oF ... | wc -l`. D1 — DEFECT, BLOCKING. AC-9's urlLink clause is vacuous: it proves nothing about urlLink. File: apps/chat/test/api.test.js:872-874. assert.match(app, /function urlLink\(tok\) \{[\s\S]*?a\.href = tok\.href;[\s\S]*?\}/, 'urlLink assigns the token href unchanged'); Both `[\s\S]*?` runs are unbounded. There are 3 occurrences of the literal `a.href = tok.href;` in app.js. On the clean file the lazy match is 170 bytes and does land inside urlLink — which is why this has only ever been seen passing. Delete the assignment from urlLink (P1) and the same regex matches a 2,617-byte span running from line 185 to line 248, swallowing appendRefLeaf, the bodyNode docblock, and finally resolving against the MARKDOWN-LINK branch's `a.href = tok.href;` at line 246. Observed: suite 203/203 green with a urlLink that sets no href at all, and 203/203 green with a urlLink that decodes it (P2). What should have happened: AC-9 says the test verifies "urlLink sets a.href = tok.href with no transformation". It does not. This is the one guard standing in for the DOM half that cannot be executed, so it is the clause with the least redundancy behind it and the most weight on it. It is also the same failure shape the CTO generalised in this task's own comment stream one stage earlier — "an assert-applied step must be scoped to the region the mutation edits, not to the file that contains it" — arriving a third time, in the test rather than in the recipe. The scoping technique that fixes it already exists 12 lines above it, in the pass-order check. Rework requirement: bound the assertion to the urlLink function body (the `indexOf` + `slice(start, indexOf('\n}\n', start))` shape already used for appendRefLeaf), assert both that the body contains `a.href = tok.href;` and that it contains no other assignment to a.href, and record predicted-vs-observed showing the clause REDDENS under both P1 (assignment deleted) and P2 (assignment wrapped in decodeURIComponent). A fix that has only been seen passing repeats the defect. I did not patch this myself. Fixing the guard whose weakness I found and then certifying my own patch is the conflict of interest this gate exists to prevent, and it is more than a typo: it changes what the suite proves. D2 — DEFECT, non-blocking; fix in the same pass, it is three lines. Terminality of url tokens has no guard at all. The pass-order guarantee has two halves: the URL pass runs first (guarded, F3b) and its tokens are terminal (unguarded). P3 deletes the `continue` at apps/chat/public/app.js:203 so a url token's text falls through into tokenizeAsRefs -> tokenizeMsgRefs -> tokenizeFileRefs after the anchor has already been appended — duplicated content in the DOM and ref links built out of text inside a URL, which is the precise thing §3.3 promises cannot happen. Suite stays 203/203. AC-9 asserts urlAt < asAt inside appendRefLeaf, which the mutation leaves true. Add one region-scoped assertion that the url branch appends and then `continue`s, and show it reddens under P3. D3 — OBSERVATION, non-blocking, no code change requested during this task. apps/chat/public/markdown.js:170 — `URL_RE.lastIndex = last;` carries the comment "REQUIRED: the trim shortened the match, and lastIndex must follow it or the tail is skipped." Deleting the line leaves the suite at 203/203 (P4), and I could not construct an input that behaves differently. Reasoning: trimUrlTail removes only characters in `.,;:!?)]}`, so the skipped tail contains only those; the character immediately after the greedy match is always whitespace, `<`, `>`, `"`, `'`, backtick, `\` or EOF; therefore no URL can begin inside the tail, and `last` is tracked separately so round-trip is unaffected either way. The line is harmless and cheap defensive coding, but the comment asserts a necessity that does not hold. Either weaken the comment to "defensive" or add the input that justifies it. Not a behaviour change I will make for you. MY OWN ATTACKS — EMITTED BYTES, not verdicts. 61 inputs, 46 url tokens, 0 violations of round-trip, slice identity, href === text, ^https?://[A-Za-z0-9], or the excluded charset. The href is the only string in this change that ever reaches an attribute; everything else is textContent/createTextNode. THE FINDING IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE ON THIS BRANCH, and the first two were caught before shipping while this one shipped inside the guard itself. A test asserts that a function assigns a token's href by matching a regex with two unbounded lazy runs across the served file. On the clean file the match is 170 bytes and does land inside the intended function, which is why it has only ever been seen passing. Delete the assignment and the same regex spans 2,617 bytes across two other functions and resolves against a DIFFERENT assignment of the same shape further down — so the suite stays fully green with a link builder that sets no href at all, and stays green again when the href is wrapped in a decode that the plan calls plan-level rework on sight.

That is the same defect as the two the implementer found in the plan's own falsification section: an assertion whose subject is the file rather than the region the mutation edits. He caught two in review of the plan and then wrote the third into a test. Worth stating as a rule rather than a third anecdote — an assertion about a function must be anchored to that function's bounds, and an unbounded lazy run between two anchors is a whole-file assertion wearing a function's name.
